Why install the CloudWatch agent on an EC2 instance?

By default, CloudWatch sees neither RAM, nor disk space, nor the instance's internal log files. The unified agent collects these system metrics (and per-process metrics with procstat) and sends the logs to CloudWatch Logs. Its configuration can be centralized in SSM Parameter Store. A correct IAM role is required, for example CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy; without the agent, no internal logs arrive in CloudWatch Logs.
How do you diagnose an agent that does not send logs?

I first check the agent version, then connectivity to the logs.<region>.amazonaws.com endpoint (Security Groups, NACLs, routing), the account/Region/log group configuration, the IAM permissions and the system time. I also consult amazon-cloudwatch-agent.log, and configuration-validation.log if the agent does not start.
What is the difference between an S3 export and a subscription?

The S3 export uses CreateExportTask and can take up to 12 hours: it is batch, for archiving. A subscription filter delivers events in real time to Kinesis Data Streams, Firehose or Lambda, including cross-account via a destination and a destination access policy. For near real time, you therefore use subscriptions, not the export.
